0.original: Bananas still weigh heavily upon Koana's mind.

48.original: I hope I have been of sufficient service to the Third Promise.

49.original: It's thanks to Wuk Evu that we were able to learn this forest's history.

50.original: That's twice now that he's helped us. To think that we might never have met him if we hadn't thought to fix the float...

51.original: Wuk Evu has given us valuable insight into the origins of xibruq pibil.

52.original: However, we are still no closer to procuring the necessary najool leaves. Unless...

53.original: Tell me─was that historic feast commemorated in some fashion? With a monument, for instance?

54.original: Indeed it was. Allow me to show you.

55.original: It is only speculation, but I dare to hope...

56.original: What does Koana want with a monument?

58.original: Offered up by the two factions, these weapons symbolize their vow that they would never again raise arms against each other.

59.original: Since this feat demands a journey through history, I thought it only logical that a monument like this might steer us true.

60.original: Especially one at the heart of so significant a battlefield.

61.original: Lamaty'i, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>─would you help me search this area for clues? Tell me if anything catches your eye.

63.original: Look here─this soil has been recently overturned.

65.original: Well, well... I would have been satisfied to find only a hint, but here they are─fresh najool leaves.

66.original: Hunmu Rruk's doing, I'd wager. There's a poetry in hiding them on this battlefield, given that it was central to the war they helped end.

69.original: Heh! So he planned all this from the start!

70.original: Thank you again, Wuk Evu. We wouldn't have found these leaves without your help.

71.original: It was my honor to render assistance.

72.original: And, with apologies to present company, allow me to offer my encouragement as well, Third Promise. Ever since I witnessed your performance in the Feat of Reeds, I have been certain that <hex:021A020203>you<hex:021A020103> are the claimant most worthy of leading our nation.

73.original: All devised solutions to the Hanuhanu's ailing crops, but you alone sought to know their culture and revive Ihih'hana, even if it seemed unrelated to your task.

74.original: In my humble opinion, no one cares more for the people of Tuliyollal and what they hold dear.

75.original: Should you again require the historical musings of an old shipwright, I am ever at your service.

76.original: For now, I take my leave.

78.original: ...We have what we need. Let us return to Iq Br'aax.

79.original: You have to wonder whether Wuk Evu is actually a historian and not a shipwright.

80.original: I'm glad we were successful. The others should be back soon, I expect.

83.original: We got the najool leaves! Wuk Evu came along and helped us find them!

84.original: Wuk Evu was here? I would have liked to say hello.

85.original: Yes, he gave us an important history lesson...

86.original: That Gulool Ja Ja brought an end to centuries of warfare surprises me little─but to achieve said peace through cuisine is something else entirely.

87.original: Leave it to my old man to find the oddest of solutions. But how about the rest of you? Is our kitchen ready?

88.original: Everything should be in order. Urianger and I made another tour of the village and borrowed the cooking utensils we need─with no mention of what we needed them <hex:021A020203>for<hex:021A020103>, of course.

89.original: And I am pleased to report that we are stocked with the finest firewood this forest had on offer.

91.original: Erenville and I found our ibruq, so we should have meat aplenty.

92.original: It was a spirited creature. So much so that its hunter fell down a cenote trying to catch it...

93.original: What part of “never speak of this to anyone” did you not understand!?

94.original: I picked a good portion of local herbs, with particular attention to the seeds that yield achiote. I'm told our resident astrologian divined the appropriate measurements for the seasoning as well.

95.original: Aye. Through further inquiry did I determine the ideal balance of spices.

96.original: Then all that remains is to prepare the dish itself. I presume that at least one among us is versed in the culinary arts?

97.original: I can hardly claim profound skill, but I have cooked for myself. You can leave the rest to me.

98.original: And you, I hope. As I recall, you are an accomplished culinarian.

99.original: And you, I hope. I could use your adventurer's grit when it comes to skinning the ibruq.

100.original: Oooh, my mouth is watering already!

102.original: I'm relieved that our dish was well received.

103.original: One final feat remains. After this one, I hardly know what to expect.

104.original: Depriving the First Promise of a keystone is a crucial victory indeed.

105.original: We need to start considering how to reclaim that keystone from Bakool Ja Ja...

106.original: That was sooo good! I'm already looking forward to having xibruq pibil again.

107.original: Here, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>. Krile made more using leftover ingredients. You'll love it!

108.original: I'm thinking to buy more for the road, myself. Now that the Feat of Repast is over, the villagers should be free to offer it to us, right?

109.original: New wares are now available from the Xbr'aal merchant in Iq Br'aax.
